outputs.explanation: The lower graph shows HMGB1 signal intensity (Nuc/Cyto) as bars with mean ± SD only (N=4 mice). With only 4 animals per group, individual data points could easily be overlaid on the bars, but none are shown.

The lower graph shows the % of aggregate-positive Purkinje cells as bars with mean ± SD (N=4 mice). Only the group means and SD are plotted; the underlying per-animal values are not shown, even though N=4 would allow this.
This panel is a Western blot image, not a quantitative plot of averaged data, so individual data points are not applicable.

This is a longitudinal line graph tracking mean ± SD rotarod time across many weeks for four groups of many animals (N=7-13); overlaying individual trajectories across so many time points and groups would be impractical and is not standard practice for this type of time-course summary plot.

These are line graphs of mean ± SD rotarod performance across days for three genotype groups at each age; as a multi-group time-course summary with many animals per group, individual data points are not expected to be overlaid.

This is a Kaplan-Meier survival curve, which is a cumulative step function derived directly from each animal's individual survival/death time; the curve itself already encodes individual-level event data, so separate individual data points are not applicable.
This panel consists of immunofluorescence micrographs, not a quantitative plot of averaged data.

Both bar graphs (molecular layer thickness and Purkinje cell number) show only mean ± SD for N=3 experiments/n=9 mice per group, without any overlaid individual data points, despite the modest sample size making this feasible.
